headline: Learned models rank protein pockets, surfaces, and ligands for candidate selection
label: Learned Candidate Prioritization Models
summary: Learned scoring of pockets, surfaces, and binding partners is narrowing candidate spaces before costly experimental or docking follow-up.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned or computational scoring that converts structural or sequence data into ranked candidate lists for downstream selection. RangeFinder constrains ligand property space from protein pockets, EpiRank retrieves epitope-like surface patches from single-chain geometry, and PSICHIC+ predicts affinity distributions from sequence and SMILES for virtual screening. Pocket coengagement scores 21,945 drug pairs by shared pocket engagement, with top-5% precision exceeding background on DDInter and KEGG DDI sets. FoXSight extracts recurring ligand-bound density from crystallographic fragment screens. What is new here is reuse of pretrained models as frozen encoders: FoldAbS adapts Protenix with lightweight heads for antibody screening, while EpiRank reports leakage controls explicitly. Not every item shares this design; the thread is ranking candidates for downstream experimental or computational follow-up.
